title: Ribasim-owned level-triggered supply with explicit capacity
purpose: Test the legacy fixed-weir supply concept without retaining a private SWAP surface-water store: the target basin level is Ribasim-owned, LevelDemand expresses the lower-level requirement, and an allocation-controlled supply route carries the capacity corresponding to WSCAP.
prerequisite: SW-RIB-SWM01-Q1A-R3L direct connector-ledger gate must pass immediately before Q1B execution.

source_semantics.legacy_capacity: WSCAP is a maximum supply capacity, not the actual supply flux

coupled_mapping.HBWEIR-WLDIP: Ribasim LevelDemand minimum level for the receiving Basin
coupled_mapping.WSCAP: maximum flow rate on the Ribasim supply route
coupled_mapping.actual q_supply: Ribasim realized physical inflow, never inferred as WSCAP by SWAP

verified_product_features: LevelDemand min_level and max_level are independently optional; missing max_level means demand-only behavior with no surplus side.
LevelDemand is evaluated by allocation at the end of the allocation time step.
LevelBoundary participates as hydraulic source in the allocation network.

frozen_model.supply_route: allocation-controlled Pump with flow_rate=0, positive route priority and case-specific max_flow_rate
frozen_model.weir_discharge: disabled in Q1B to isolate supply semantics
frozen_model.allocation_semantics: one-sided lower LevelDemand at -0.2 m, evaluated at end of 86400 s allocation interval

comparators: direct cumulative physical supply volume from model.integrator.u.pump
zero supply when already above the legacy-equivalent supply target
direct mass residual = Basin storage change - Pump cumulative supply
anti_equivalence_warning: LevelDemand is not declared byte-for-byte equivalent to legacy WLEVBAL. Q1B tests the physically intended fixed-weir supply envelope only. Allocation forecast and timing semantics remain Ribasim semantics and must be reported explicitly.
pass_meaning: Bounded evidence that the fixed-weir WLDIP/WSCAP supply envelope can be externalized into Ribasim-owned demand and capacity without a duplicate SWAP surface-water state or hidden actual-supply flux.
fail_meaning: The simple mapping WLDIP -> lower level demand and WSCAP -> route capacity is insufficient under the tested Ribasim allocation semantics.
nonclaims: No scarcity competition between multiple users.
No fixed-weir discharge in the same test.
design_rationale: The legacy WLDIP supply rule is one-sided: it requests supply below HBWEIR-WLDIP but does not create a surplus demand above that level.
Therefore Q1B uses only LevelDemand.min_level and leaves max_level missing.
A positive route-priority cost ensures unnecessary supply flow is disfavored after the higher-priority demand objective is satisfied.
The capacity-limited case deliberately tests that unmet lower-level demand remains visible rather than being hidden by a SWAP-side storage floor.

direct_ledger_authority.statement: Pump has one cumulative horizontal-flow state with derivative equal to physical Pump flow.
direct_ledger_authority.anti_tautology: Q1B does not infer supplied volume from Basin storage; it compares Basin storage change to the independently integrated Pump state.

execution_contract: In the closure workflow Q1B is a later step after R3L; shell fail-fast semantics prevent Q1B from executing if R3L fails.
